To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Plastic waste is the worst waste management option for human health, as well as for the environment, due to its high toxicity and persistence”.

“Plastics in the urban setting are a significant source of exposure to toxic chemicals, which can induce adverse health effects, such as endocrine disruption, reproductive disorders, metabolic syndrome and even neurotoxicity, with the landfilling option being the worst management strategy”.

Landfilling plastic waste is the worst option in terms of health risk, whereas the best options for management of plastic waste are the ones that combine waste treatment coupled with material or energy recovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new tool that can help decision makers and policy makers identify and quantify the health effects of plastic waste management strategies and thus, inform their decisions on the selection of the most appropriate waste management strategy.
the development and application of a novel methodology that can be applied to the assessment of the environmental health risks associated with the life cycle of plastics in urban areas.
the health impacts of the plastic waste crisis and provides an innovative approach that can be used to inform policy and decision making in the area of sustainable plastic waste management.

plastic waste management strategies should be prioritized in the direction of waste prevention and recycling, while landfilling should be considered as the last resort option.

the use of plastic products and the management practices of plastic waste in Greece, are associated with adverse health effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of plastics in our daily life has a significant impact on our health, and that we should take this into account in our decision making process.

the use of plastic products and their disposal in landfills and incinerators is the main source of persistent organic pollutants (POPs), and the main route of exposure to these pollutants is the ingestion of contaminated food.

the health risks associated with the use, disposal and management of plastic are real, significant and should be considered when developing policies for plastic management.
the plastic crisis is a public health crisis, which needs to be addressed in a holistic way.
plastic waste is a serious threat to public health, especially when it is landfilled.
